findings.pdf_says: Format 1 (delimited):   IF condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ ELSE statement-2 ] END-IF   — with IF, ELSE and END-IF UNDERLINED and THEN, statement-1, statement-2 NOT underlined.
findings.markdown_says: IF condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ ELSE statement-2 ] END-IF   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27465 — no <u> markup on any word)
findings.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2 an underlined word in a general format is a REQUIRED word and a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word. This figure mixes both: IF / ELSE / END-IF are required, THEN is optional. With every underline dropped the required-vs-optional distinction is unrecoverable from the markdown, and a reader deriving the grammar from it cannot tell that THEN may be omitted while END-IF may not. The transcription DOES have a convention for this — 14.9.17.2 on page 660 renders '<u>GO</u> TO ... <u>DEPENDING</u> ON identifier-1' — so this is an omission, not a house style.
findings.suggested_repair: Restore the underlines using the existing convention: '<u>IF</u> condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ <u>ELSE</u> statement-2 ] <u>END-IF</u>'.

findings.pdf_says: Format 2 (historic):   IF condition-1 THEN { statement-1 / NEXT SENTENCE } [ ELSE { statement-2 / NEXT SENTENCE } ]   — with IF, NEXT, SENTENCE (both occurrences) and ELSE UNDERLINED; THEN, statement-1, statement-2 NOT underlined.
findings.markdown_says: IF condition-1 THEN { statement-1 / NEXT SENTENCE } [ ELSE { statement-2 / NEXT SENTENCE } ]   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27469 — no <u> markup on any word)
findings.why_it_matters: Same required-word loss as Format 1, and here it also erases that NEXT and SENTENCE are each individually underlined (both are required words of the NEXT SENTENCE phrase). The brace/bracket structure and the ASCII '/' rendering of the stacked alternatives are faithful; only the underlining is lost.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.15.2 General format:   FREE { data-name-1 } ...   — FREE is UNDERLINED (verified by rendering page 657 at 300 dpi and cropping the figure; the underline spans all four letters).
findings.why_it_matters: FREE is a required word; without the underline the figure formally reads as if FREE were an optional word (5.2.6.2). The braces and the trailing ellipsis (which correctly binds to the closing brace per 5.2.7) are transcribed correctly, so this is the only defect in the figure. The markdown already uses <u> in neighbouring formats (14.9.17.2, 14.9.18.2), so the loss is local.

findings.pdf_says: General rule 1) b) 3. reads 'If the LAST phrase is specified one of the following occurs:' with sub-items 'a.' (starting on page 662, continuing at the top of page 663 with '3 exception for EC-USER ...') and 'b. If no exception condition is raised, the RAISING phrase is ignored and no exception condition is set to exist in the activating runtime element.' — both printed at the fourth indent level, subordinate to item 3.
findings.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 27416 and 27418 are both at column 0: '3 exception for EC-USER and that exception condition is not specified ...' and 'b. If no exception condition is raised, the RAISING phrase is ignored ...', while their sibling 'a.' on page 662 (line 27403) is indented nine spaces.
findings.why_it_matters: The zero indentation detaches sub-item b. (and the tail of sub-item a.) from their parent list item 1) b) 3. When rendered, b. becomes a top-level paragraph and the reader loses the fact that it is the second alternative of 'If the LAST phrase is specified one of the following occurs' — i.e. the condition under which the RAISING phrase is ignored. The transcription lost the nesting at the page break.
findings.suggested_repair: Indent lines 27416 and 27418 to nine spaces so they match the indentation of sibling item 'a.' at line 27403.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.14.4  General rules  — a fourth-level clause heading, one level below 14.9.14 EXIT statement, identical in rank to 14.9.15.4, 14.9.16.4 and 14.9.17.4.
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.14.4 General rules   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27107 — level 2, the same level as '## 14.9.14 EXIT statement' at line 27013, whereas '### 14.9.15.4 General rules' at line 27170 is level 3)
findings.why_it_matters: The heading is promoted a level, so General rules for the EXIT statement renders as a sibling of the EXIT statement clause itself instead of a child. That breaks the generated outline/TOC nesting and any tooling that walks the markdown heading tree to map clause numbers to sections.
findings.suggested_repair: Demote line 27107 to '### 14.9.14.4 General rules' to match the 14.9.15.x / 14.9.16.x / 14.9.17.x pattern. (Line 27058, '## 14.9.14.3 Syntax rules', has the same defect on page 654 — outside this batch.)

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.18.4  General rules  — a fourth-level clause heading under 14.9.18 GOBACK statement, identical in rank to 14.9.18.1/.2/.3.
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.18.4 General rules   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27389 — level 2, while its siblings '### 14.9.18.1 General', '### 14.9.18.2 General format' and '### 14.9.18.3 Syntax rules' are level 3)
findings.why_it_matters: Within a single clause the four sub-clauses are transcribed at two different heading levels, so General rules renders as a sibling of the GOBACK statement clause rather than as its fourth sub-clause. The outline nesting and clause-to-section mapping are wrong.

findings.pdf_says: 14.9.19.4  General rules  — a fourth-level clause heading under 14.9.19 IF statement, identical in rank to 14.9.19.1/.2/.3.
findings.markdown_says: ## 14.9.19.4 General rules   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 27501 — level 2, while '### 14.9.19.1 General', '### 14.9.19.2 General formats' and '### 14.9.19.3 Syntax rules' are level 3)
findings.why_it_matters: Same promotion defect: General rules for the IF statement renders as a sibling of the IF statement clause instead of a child, corrupting the heading tree.
